## Summary

Implemented SPEC.md section 4 (Health/HealthKit) for the Health screen:

- **`App_Resources/iOS/app.entitlements`** (new) — `com.apple.developer.healthkit` capability
- **`App_Resources/iOS/Info.plist`** — added `NSHealthShareUsageDescription` / `NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription`
- **`app/services/health-kit.ts`** (new) — direct `HKHealthStore` calls (no wrapper plugin): authorization status/request, saving a 500-step sample, and a 7-day daily-sum query via `HKStatisticsQuery`
- **`app/components/Health.vue`** — wired status line, Request Access / Log 500 Steps buttons, and the Last 7 Days list to the service, refreshing on `navigatingTo`
- **`types/references.d.ts`** — added a reference to `objc!HealthKit.d.ts`, since the default `@nativescript/types` common subset excludes HealthKit

Along the way, verified the full flow live on the iOS Simulator (via `idb`) and caught two real bugs that only surfaced at runtime:
1. `HKStatisticsQuery` returns an `HKErrorNoData` error (not a nil-sum result) when no samples of a type exist anywhere yet — now handled as 0 steps.
2. NativeScript's iOS JS engine ignores `toLocaleDateString`/`toLocaleString` locale options — replaced with manual weekday/month arrays and a manual thousands-separator formatter.

Confirmed: grant flow, deny flow (status `denied`, buttons disabled, list shows "Health access needed", no crash), double-tap logging → `1,000 steps (today)`, data persists across relaunch, and back navigation — all matching SPEC.md §4 label text exactly. `ns build ios` succeeds cleanly with no type errors.
